statement: V10: every shipped sentence, voice file and derived list carries a resolved licence compatible with AGPL redistribution. Gate: corpora_shippable is an allow-list; anything unclassified fails; NC and ND sources are excluded at ingest, not at package time.
why_this_corpus_exists: The obvious test — 'no forbidden sentence appears in the output' — is passed by a pipeline that downloads TED2020, parses it and drops the rows at the end. That pipeline has already written CC BY-NC-ND text into every intermediate artefact and onto the build machine's disk, which is what 'at ingest, not at package time' forbids. So every `refused` case below is asserted against a transport that records every request and MUST have recorded none, and every `permitted` case is asserted to actually mint a permit, so the gate cannot pass by refusing everything.
source: ~/duolingo-research/deep/00-EDGE-CASES.md EC-PACK-09..13; deep/10 §S2 and its adversarial review R2, R3, R4, R7, R8

cases.why: The TED Talks Usage Policy is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. NC bites because an AGPL app can be forked commercially; ND bites because every exercise shape — word bank, cloze, re-ordering, synthesised audio — is a derivative. deep/10 listed TED2020 in its quality-first ingest order and then reversed it; the reversal is the case.
Not an es-only cut. TED2020 carries 296k-417k pairs on all four v1 pairs and is forbidden on all four.

R8. The OPUS legacy page says 'For commercial use, please contact NTT Communication Science Laboratories' — the same non-commercial-by-default category that cut TED2020. deep/10 put 25,740,836 ja pairs in its corpus table and gave the corpus no verdict anywhere, which is exactly how a build script templated from that table picks it up.

The legacy page states no licence at all; it asks for a link back, and a request is not a grant. The allow-list is an ALLOW-list, so 'no licence stated' fails rather than defaults. It remains usable as an oracle over data somebody else already holds — it is never ingested through this door.

Same. And R2 measured CCMatrix v1 and NLLB v1 as byte-identical alignment_pairs on all four pairs, so the licensed route to the same bitext is `nllb` — which is why substituting it is a decision with a reason rather than a fallback.

EC-PACK-12. NC data may ride inside a CC BY-NC-SA pack and may never be ingested as shippable text; G2 consults it on the build machine. That it is refused HERE, at the corpus door, is the point — the NC-vs-AGPL agony belongs at ingest.

A source nobody put in config.SOURCES has no licence verdict, and a source with no verdict must never be read. The refusal names every registered source so the operator sees what they could have meant.
Attribution-only, so every shipped sentence needs a credits row reachable from S152 (INV-PACK-17). Present so the gate cannot pass by refusing everything.

R2: the NLLB legacy page was never fetched by deep/10 and it states ODC-By 1.0. The plan ingests it, capped, for selection and validation statistics, and keeps it oracle-only while the crawl-text copyright question is open (plan risk 2). 'May not be shipped' and 'may not be ingested' are different decisions and this case pins the difference.

R4, re-verified live 2026-09-12 by Content-Length: spa_sentences_CC0.tsv.bz2 is 2,266 bytes (deu 1,852, jpn 228, fra 313,297). The CC0 route is not a way to avoid the credits screen for es/de/ja; it is a way to have no course. Listed for fr only, and the refusal for es must name the language rather than the licence.
The one language where the subset is a real pool — and even there it is a sub-pool of `tatoeba`.
